approachQuestion.prompt: Input is an absolute Unix path of at most 200,000 ASCII characters. Split on slash; ignore empty components and "."; for "..", remove the most recent normal component if one exists, otherwise stay at root. Other components are names. Return "/" followed by surviving names joined by one slash. Example "/a/./b/../c//" -> "/a/c"; "/../../" -> "/".

options.text: Scan components left to right with a stack; ignore empty and dot, pop for dot-dot if possible, otherwise push the name.
options.feedback: For "/a/b/../../c", both parent components must be applied in order, yielding "/c".

options.text: First remove empty and dot components. Repeatedly find the leftmost dot-dot, delete it and the preceding normal component if any (or just it at root), shift the remaining components, and restart. Join the survivors.
options.feedback: Repeated string rescans implement the same rules but revisit components and shift text.
Sorting changes path meaning; /a/b and /b/a are distinct paths.

options.text: Keep every normal component and ignore both dot and dot-dot components.
options.feedback: For /a/b/../c, this returns /a/b/c, but dot-dot must remove b, producing /a/c.

feedback.reason: For "/a/b/../../c", both parent components must be applied in order, yielding "/c".

Apply parent components in order. A dot-dot removes the latest surviving directory, while at root it does nothing; names merely containing dots remain ordinary names. Repeated slashes contribute empty components, not directories.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For path-component-normalization-optimal, let n be the number of input commands or tokens. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Input is immutable; output storage is excluded.
constraints: Every stack push/pop and fixed-size operation takes constant time. The implementation is iterative; call-stack space is O(1).
The input may force a stack containing a linear number of entries. No hidden copying of the entire input occurs.

Here n is the number of ASCII characters. Components are scanned once; store source spans or copy each name once. Joining copies each surviving character once. Working component spans and name buffers count; the returned string is excluded.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Path scanning and component-stack processing have linear total character work.
details: Scanning components, stack updates, and writing the canonical path have linear total character work. A path of ordinary names can retain a linear number of components until completion.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A path with many ordinary components retains their names/locations until later parent components or final output; this stack grows with path length.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each component is pushed once or pops one surviving directory, and total name/output character work is linear in path length.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A final path component may change the canonical result, so all path characters may need inspection.
